claim: On layouts where each team starts with 2 dragons, main sometimes has at most 6 dragons alive at raw round 100 while the opponent has at least 15, and loses almost all of those games; it does not happen on other layouts.
how_to_count: Take every game whose replay stores one of our main submission ids (18066, 18068, 18504, 18570) on our side. Use the layout's initial DRAGON rows to count starting dragons per team; keep layouts with exactly 2 per team. Rebuild the true state and take the number of living dragons per side after all events of raw round 100 (zero-based roundStart index 100); skip games that ended before that round. Stall = ours <= 6 and theirs >= 15. Count stall games, how many of them we won, and split by the battle's opponentElo (1700-1899, 1900-2099, 2100+). Count the reverse case (theirs <= 6 and ours >= 15). Repeat the stall count on main games on all other layouts. In the stall games also give the median number of pearls each side ate in raw rounds 0-100 (a pearl is credited to the dragon whose turn removed it). PART B (cause). For main games on Tower Defense #1 that reached raw round 100: after each of raw rounds 0 to 50, take the heads of our living dragons and every pearl on the board, and compute the shortest path in steps from any of our heads to any pearl, where a step may not cross a kelp edge (EDGE kind 1), a portal edge (kind 2) leads to the tile beyond its partner edge, the board wraps, and dragon bodies are ignored. Take the median over the 51 rounds per game, then the median over games; do the same for the opponent. Also count pearls eaten by each side in raw rounds 0-100 per game (median over games).

claim: On layouts where the queen can leave her spawn, our queen's death is by wall or own body in about twice as many main games as their queen's.
how_to_count: Main games only (ids as in F7). Exclude the three layouts where queen_spawn_dead_end is true in maps.json (Schooltime #1, Schooltime #2, Slithery Fight #1). The queen of a side is its lowest initial dragon id. A game counts for a side if that queen has a dragonDeath event with engine reason 0 (wall) or 1 (own body). Count games for our queen and for their queen, in total and for: opponentElo 1700-1899; opponentElo 1900-2099; the first 97 and the last 98 main games when all 195 main games are ordered by (game completedAt, game id), each then filtered to the non-excluded layouts.

claim: Of the pearls dropped in cross-team head-on meetings and eaten within 15 rounds, we eat about 40 percent and the opponent about 60 percent, in every slice.
how_to_count: Main games only (ids as in F7). A cross-team head-on meeting is a pair of dragonDeath events with engine reason 3 (head-on) in the same action, one dragon from each team. The pearls that appear on body segments 0, 2, 4, ... of both dead dragons are the drop pearls (ceil(length/2) each). For each drop pearl find the dragon that removes it; if that happens at a raw round no more than 15 after the drop round (same round counts), credit that dragon's side. Sum credited pearls for us and for them over both sides' drops. Share = us / (us + them). Report for all main games, for opponentElo 1700-1899 and 1900-2099, and for the first 97 and last 98 main games ordered by (game completedAt, game id). Also count games where we were credited fewer, more, or the same number as them.
